title: Common-stage spectra and residue degrees of sheet return
statement: Fix D, m≥1, X₀ separated finite type over k₀, ℓ≠p and an algebraic closure Ω/Q_ℓ. Let R be any functor between the two actual common-stage Weil hearts satisfying the specified sheet-return carrier and structure formula [def-zl-constant-extension-sheet-pullback-data]. Assume the rational intertwining and scalar-compatibility predicates of [def-zl-sheet-return-data] for every finite coefficient field E. At each closed point z of X₀×k₀ k_m the two punctual eigenvalue predicates [def-weil-punctual-weights] agree for each α∈Ω; the degree over k₀ is m times the degree over k_m and #κ(z)=q^(m deg_km(z)); and the two degree-zero local operators are conjugate as required by ConstantExtensionLocalConjugacy [def-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-data], for every finite presentation and residue embedding. The lemma has no assertion about pure weights or finite filtrations.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp. 150--152, and (1.2.6), p. 154; ordered block and finite-filtration consequences.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $z$ and choose compatible geometric points $x:s\to X$ and $y=j_0x:s\to Y$ arising from a residue embedding extending $k_m\subset k$. The closed-point field lemma applies because $X_{0,m}$ is finite type over $k_m$, so $r=[\kappa(z):k_m]$ is finite and positive. An $r$-element basis gives a bijection of sets $\kappa(z)\simeq k_m^r$; hence $\#\kappa(z)=(q^m)^r=q^{mr}$. Multiplying a basis of $k_m/k_0$ by this basis gives $[\kappa(z):k_0]=mr$. The local-operator definition therefore uses $mr$ transitions in the $k_0$ interpretation and $r$ transitions in the $k_m$ interpretation. Write $h=g_s$; the two point returns are $H^{mr}y=yh^{mr}$ and $(g_X^m)^rx=x(h^m)^r$. They are the same square after composing with $j_0$, since $H^mj_0=j_0g_X^m$.

proof.text: Descend the object, its structure map and comparison to a common finite coefficient field. Apply the assumed rational intertwining and its scalar compatibility there; take degree-zero fibre cohomology and extend scalars. For arbitrary residue embeddings use the following conjugacy comparison. The inverse linear isomorphism carries eigenvectors back, proving equality of the existential common-stage spectra.

proof.text: For any other residue embedding and its associated geometric point, apply the local-conjugacy statement at a common finite rational stage to $N$ over $k_0$, and to $R(N)$ over $k_m$. Both models are finite type over their stated finite fields. It gives intertwining isomorphisms $a$ and $b$ from the previously chosen stalks to the new ones. The new comparison $a c b^{-1}$ then intertwines the new local operators, since $(a c b^{-1})F'_R=a c F_R b^{-1}=a F_N c b^{-1}=F'_N(a c b^{-1})$. Scalar compatibility from step 7 passes this to $\Qlb$. Thus the operator assertion is independent up to conjugacy of the choices of residue embedding and associated geometric point; it does not presume those points to be literally fixed by Frobenius.
